baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction joins qarinuhu, the deictic hadha ma ladayya, and atid.
baseline_models.mechanism: A continuously attached companion speaks to place a presently held, already prepared referent before an addressee.

activation_trace.role: The paired companion supplies the enduring possessor-presenter rather than a chance observer.
Present preparedness makes the held referent available for immediate presentation.
Overt utterance performs the presentation.

changed_reading.before: A companion makes a vague report about something ready.
changed_reading.after: An attached companion formally presents what is already in his keeping and prepared.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Qala plus hadha ma ladayya can function as an identifying gesture, while atid marks prior preparation.
baseline_models.mechanism: The saying points out and delimits a prepared item; it does not merely describe the companion's inventory.

activation_trace.role: A thing's saying as indication makes the utterance deictically identify its referent.
Binding supplies a stable relation between presenter and presented item.
The split-root image of prepared equipment sharpens prior arrangement for a coming need.

changed_reading.before: This is a static statement of possession.
changed_reading.after: This is a deictic tender: the speech identifies a bound, prearranged item now made available.

context_deltas.mechanism: Preserved writing, seated reception, vigilant custody, repeated readiness, and witnessing turn the companion's possession into the endpoint of continuous collection and preservation.

activation_trace.role: The companion anchors the final custodial presenter in the focus ayah.
The written object supplies a durable recordable medium.
Guarding preserves that medium against loss.
Receiving speech as something taken supplies the collection stage.
Watchful guarding gives the collected speech a custodian.
The earlier ready attendant makes focus readiness continuous rather than last-minute.
Knowledge-bearing testimony supplies the evidentiary endpoint.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from two seated receivers in 50:17, through monitored utterance in 50:18, to an arriving witness in 50:21 and the companion's presentation in 50:23.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies preservation, reception, guarding, readiness, and witness; I infer a chain from collection to tender, while the live alternative is that the companion presents the person rather than a record.

changed_reading.before: The companion happens to have an unspecified ready item.
changed_reading.after: The companion closes a chain of custody by tendering preserved, continuously gathered evidence.

context_deltas.mechanism: A driven self arrives with driver and witness, then a dual command orders casting; focus binding and readiness can therefore make the companion an escort handing over a detainee.

activation_trace.role: Binding one entity to another anchors custodial accompaniment.
Immediate availability marks the escorted referent as ready for transfer.
Driving and impelling supply coercive movement into the scene.
A co-present observer supplies the second escort-side function.
Casting supplies the ordered destination and completes the handoff.

structural_cues: 50:21 gives every self two accompanying roles, and 50:24 immediately follows the focus with a dual imperative.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies driver, witness, arrival, and a dual casting command; I infer that the speaking companion belongs to that custody team and that hadha points to the escorted person, while a dossier remains a live alternative.

changed_reading.before: The companion presents an object or record.
changed_reading.after: The companion may be an escort reporting the bound person's arrival and readiness for judicial transfer.

context_deltas.mechanism: Removal of a cover and newly penetrating sight immediately precede the companion's hadha, so the utterance identifies an already present reality that has only now become apprehensible.

activation_trace.role: Speech as indication anchors the companion's utterance as a pointing act.
Prior presence means the referent need not have just arrived.
Lifting a cover supplies the transition from hidden to disclosed.
Actual seeing makes the disclosed referent available to the deictic this.

structural_cues: 50:22 and 50:23 are adjacent and repeat hadha across unveiling and presentation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies uncovering, sight, adjacency, and repeated hadha; I infer continuity of the newly apprehensible field, while the companion could still introduce a separate referent.

changed_reading.before: The companion brings new information or a newly arrived item.
changed_reading.after: The companion points out what was already present and prepared but had remained outside the addressee's sight.

context_deltas.mechanism: The companion speaks again to deny causal responsibility, disputation is barred, prior warning has been advanced, and the operative word cannot be replaced; the focus presentation becomes an opening submission in an adversarial proceeding.

activation_trace.role: The paired speaker anchors continuity with the focus presenter.
The repeated companion now speaks defensively, activating a party-like role.
A second overt statement turns presentation into an exchange of submissions.
Dispute among opposing parties supplies the adversarial frame.
Advancing beforehand makes the warning procedurally prior to the present exchange.
Blocked substitution makes the governing statement fixed rather than negotiable.

structural_cues: 50:27 repeats qala qarinuhu, while 50:28 repeats ladayya and continues the speech exchange begun at the focus.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated companion speech, opposing claims, prior warning, and a fixed word; I infer that 50:23 is a formal tender, while the 50:27 companion may be a different companion or role.

changed_reading.before: The companion is a neutral attendant making a simple report.
changed_reading.after: The companion's presentation opens an adjudicative exchange in which evidence is tendered and responsibility is contested.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the surrounding scene strongly supports external attendants, but q-r-n explicitly permits a self paired with the body and 50:16 supplies hidden self-speech; render only as a possible personification of an internal co-agent, not as an identification of the companion.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Qarinuhu is anchored through the q-r-n branch of a self paired with the body, and qala can externalize what was formerly inward.

activation_trace.role: The self paired with the body permits an internal companion reading.
Unexpressed speech held in the self supplies latent content now voiced.
Hidden self-talk supplies the earlier internal speech process.
The inward rational-affective content supplies a carrier for that hidden speech.

changed_reading.before: An external companion reports what he holds.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the embodied inner self becomes a speaking companion that externalizes the hidden content it has carried.

strongest_changes: Continuous reception, guarding, readiness, and witness transform possession into a chain-of-custody tender.
Immediate unveiling turns hadha into recognition of an already present reality.
Driver-witness accompaniment and the dual casting command keep a detainee-handoff reading alive beside the record reading.
The later companion dispute recasts the presentation as an adversarial submission.
summary.what_was_special: The focus acts as a hinge: a paired presence turns prior monitoring into a deictic handoff, yet the packet sustains record, escorted person, revealed reality, and litigating companion as distinct mechanisms.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not settle whether the deictic referent is a record, deeds, the escorted person, or another prepared entity.
It remains uncertain whether the companion of 50:27 is identical with the companion of 50:23.
The addressees of the dual command are not explicitly identified within the focus construction.
